messages:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a perfetto capture on the dedicated pool to investigate kernel-selection hot paths and a bunch of kernel timeline slices are missing lineinfo for runtime.so (shows <unknown> at several addresses). built with -g and split DWARF, so confused.

maria: hmm. did you do the capture inside the same container as the runtime? we had issues before when debug files lived on the host only.

alex: captured from host (nsenter into container pid) but using perfetto UI on the host. command I used:
```
perfetto --txt -o /tmp/trace.pbperfetto
# trace config: gpu+vitals+thread_time
```
output snippet:
```
Kernel timeline: cudaLaunchKernel at 0x7f3a1b2f <unknown>
kernel duration 1.2ms
...
```
addr2line on the host returns symbols for same build-id, but inside container addr2line can't find the file.

samir: likely build-id path mismatch or missing /usr/lib/debug inside container. distroless image strips debug files so nsys/perfetto only sees addresses. try bind-mounting host debug files into container: `-v /usr/lib/debug:/usr/lib/debug:ro` or copy `*.debug` into /usr/lib/debug/. Also check build-id symlink tree.

tim: also check that build was not post-processed by objcopy in CI (we had a step that ran `strip --strip-debug` and `objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink` sometimes moved ids). if build-id differs then addr2line will fail.

maria: another thing — CUPTI/nvtx interaction. if you captured with nsys earlier and got lines but perfetto doesn't, maybe nsys injects additional info. nsys sometimes fetches debug info differently. did you run `nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx` vs full capture?

alex: i can repro with `nsys profile --output /tmp/nsys` — results are inconsistent. sometimes nsys shows source lines, sometimes not. ci-bot flagged a perf regression yesterday which triggered this.

ci-bot: alert: perf-regression #4523 triggered on branch `opt/batching-heuristics` — 7% P99 increase. linked trace: s3://redwood-traces/1717592468/trace.pbperfetto

jen: quick diagnostics checklist:
- verify `readelf --note=.note.gnu.build-id -n runtime.so` inside container matches host runtime.so
- confirm `/usr/lib/debug/.build-id` contains the elf's debug file
- run `eu-readelf`/`eu-strip` steps in CI to ensure debuglink created correctly
- try `gdb --batch -ex "info sources" -ex quit runtime.so` inside container

alex: ran the readelf check — build-id differs between host artifact and container artifact (CI packaging step replaces runtime.so with stripped version and uploads separate debug file). so that explains missing lines when using the container-provided runtime.

samir: fix options: ensure CI preserves build-id during packaging or copy the correct debug file into the image at build time. short-term workaround: mount the correct debug file path into the container before profiling, e.g. `docker run -v /ci/artifacts/runtime-<buildid>.debug:/usr/lib/debug/.build-id/7f/3a1b2f...debug:ro`. ugly but works for repro.

maria: note about overlayfs: our container runner uses overlay mounts which change inode numbers and in rare cases perf tools fail to resolve build-id via /proc/self/map_files. mounting as a real directory (not overlay) fixed a similar case last year.

alex: re-ran perfetto after bind-mounting debug files and using nsys with `--capture=all` and now kernel timeline shows resolved source lines for those kernel wrappers (woo!). p99 trace now points at batch selection code not GPU init path — looks like the batching heuristic change is the actual culprit.

jen: can you paste the minimal repro steps so we can add to the bug and CI test? include exact docker run, mount, and profiler flags.

alex: dropping steps here:
```
# run container with debug files mounted
docker run --rm -it \
  -v /ci/artifacts/runtime-7f3a1b2f.debug:/usr/lib/debug/.build-id/7f/3a/1b2f.debug:ro \
  -v /host/traces:/traces:rw \
  --entrypoint /bin/bash redwood/runtime:opt-batching

# inside container
nsys profile --capture=all -o /traces/nsys.raw --trace=file,osrt --stats true ./bin/runtime --run-batch-repro

# convert for perfetto UI (if needed)
nsys export --format=pprof /traces/nsys.raw -o /traces/for_perfetto
```
this gave resolved sources in perfetto and confirmed the hotspot.

tim: great. long-term we should add CI step that generates a small perfetto trace and verifies lineinfo resolves (smoke test). also add a packaging lint that ensures debug build-id sync.

alex: filing bug now with repro and attaching trace + diff. thanks all :thumbsup:
